title: Check Foundry VTT system-package licensing case by case (owner proposed reusing GURPS specifically), and propose a consolidated system-agnostic architecture for rendering/turns/combat/vision/limitations
objective: Owner proposed reusing free Foundry VTT system packages (e.g. GURPS) since Foundry's core is proprietary but community systems are separately licensed, and asked how to consolidate rendering/turns/combat/vision/limitations in a system-agnostic way. Researched via WebSearch: (1) GURPS Foundry implementations (crnormand/gurps and similar) are distributed under permission from Steve Jackson Games' Online Policy specifically for personal use with owned GURPS books -- NOT a true open-source license, and risky for the owner's stated closed-source-commercial-sale goal; this corrects the owner's specific example. (2) By contrast, the official dnd5e Foundry system's code is MIT and its SRD 5.1 game content is CC-BY-4.0 (Wizards of the Coast's own open license) -- a genuinely safe, cleanly-licensed combination. (3) pf2e's code is Apache-2.0, but its content licensing involves a specific Foundry Gaming LLC/Paizo partnership agreement that may not transfer to third-party reuse -- a middle case needing further verification before relying on its content. (4) Licensing is a case-by-case, two-axis question (code license vs. game-content license) per system/publisher, not a blanket 'Foundry modules are free' assumption. (5) Foundry's own CORE architecture patterns (Active Effects' key-path + Change-Mode modifier system with a fixed application order; Combat/Combatant's initiative-sorted turn tracker with pluggable comparator; the DataModel/template.json per-system schema pattern; VisionSource's point-source polygon visibility computation) are extensively documented in Foundry's public API docs -- these are safe to study and reimplement fresh in Rust as design patterns (same treatment as Sylves/Townscaper: study the pattern, build a clean-room implementation, no code or copyrighted content touched, so no attribution entry needed) regardless of Foundry core's proprietary status, since documented API concepts/behavior are not the same as copyrighted source code. Proposed a consolidated architecture answering the owner's actual question: a generic Rust core (modifier/active-effect system, turn/initiative tracker, vision/LOS polygon computation, ECS-based flexible entity schema) that any specific TTRPG system plugs into via its own schema/dice-formulas/custom-modifier-hooks, with rendering (Three.js) staying a pure consumer -- all flowing through the existing Command/DomainEvent/Snapshot pipeline.
validations: Added a 'Foundry system-package licensing is case by case' section to docs/research/vtt-rules-and-character-system-options.md: corrects the owner's specific GURPS example (SJG Online Policy, personal-use-only, not open source) with concrete evidence, contrasts it against dnd5e (MIT code + CC-BY-4.0 SRD content, genuinely safe) and pf2e (Apache-2.0 code, partnership-specific content licensing needing more verification), and states the general two-axis (code license vs. content license) rule for evaluating any future system.

Added a 'Foundry's core architecture patterns (safe to study, never a code source)' section documenting Active Effects (key-path + Change Mode: Add/Multiply/Override/Upgrade/Downgrade/Custom, fixed application order), Combat/Combatant (initiative-sorted turn tracker, pluggable comparator), the DataModel/template.json per-system schema pattern, and VisionSource (point-source polygon visibility) -- framed explicitly as documented-API-concept study, not code reuse, consistent with how Sylves and Townscaper were already treated in this planning process.

Added a 'Proposed consolidated agnostic architecture' section directly answering the owner's question: how rendering, turns, combat, vision, and limitations consolidate through the existing Command/DomainEvent/Snapshot pipeline and the already-flagged ECS crates (hecs/specs), with vision/LOS computation specifically tied to the existing Isekai/Wasm pathway (matching both Foundry's and PlanarAlly's own architecture for that specific piece).

Updated docs/research/RESEARCH-DECISIONS-REGISTRY.md's VTT rules and character system section with rows for the dnd5e/pf2e/GURPS licensing findings and the Foundry-core-patterns-as-reference-only framing.

No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR reopened -- documentation research/proposal only; the proposed architecture is explicitly a proposal, not a decision, consistent with this document's non-normative status.
risks: Licensing findings reflect sources checked today (2026-08-01) and are inherently fact-specific per publisher/system -- any future system considered for content reuse needs its own explicit re-check, not reliance on this document's examples alone.
The proposed consolidated architecture is a design proposal only, not validated by any spike or prototype -- recorded as such.
No dependency installed, no code written -- research/documentation only.
